misconceptions.description: Judging tools by how many features they list rather than how well each tool serves the specific learning task
misconceptions.trigger: learner recommends the tool with the longest feature list without tying features to the task
misconceptions.feedback: Count fit, not features. A tool wins the audit when it best serves the defined task, even if it has fewer features than a rival.

misconceptions.description: Comparing tools on different dimensions each so no head-to-head judgment is actually possible
misconceptions.trigger: learner praises Tool A for price and Tool B for accessibility without scoring both on the same criteria
misconceptions.feedback: Define one shared criteria set and score every tool against all of it. Praising each tool on a different axis is not a comparison.

misconceptions.description: Naming a single best tool as if it were best for every context, ignoring learners, budget, and setting
misconceptions.trigger: learner declares a universal winner without naming the context the recommendation holds for
misconceptions.feedback: There is no context-free best tool. State the learners, setting, and constraints your recommendation assumes, so a reader can tell when it would change.
